title: Read consistency, indexes, and projections
purpose: Find stale, inconsistent, incomplete, or misleading read results caused by consistency modes, projection lag, indexing, pagination, rebuild, or cache boundaries.
invariants: Strong/consistent reads must not return state older than the consistency barrier they claim to enforce.
Stale reads may lag only within their documented semantics and must never be mislabeled as strong.
Primary-store and rebuildable read projections must converge to the same business truth represented by committed history.
Projection rebuild or index catch-up must not expose silently incomplete results as complete.
Pagination must not duplicate, omit, or reorder records beyond documented cursor semantics when writes occur concurrently.
Filters and aggregates must produce results consistent with the same snapshot/consistency boundary as the surrounding query.

The read surfaces a request pins — the main-store read handle (dal.Store.NewReadHandle), the read-store snapshot (readstore.NewSnapshot / query.AlignedIndexSnapshot), and request-local query state — must obey the same consistency contract as an unpinned read at the same barrier.
Read-path failover or leader changes must not weaken the requested consistency mode.
adversarial_questions: Which reads actually execute a ReadIndex/barrier and which intentionally do not?
Can a consistency header/mode be dropped between HTTP/gRPC and the query controller?
Can an index watermark advance before all represented rows are queryable?
Can rebuild expose an empty or partial index while reporting readiness?
Can cursor pagination cross snapshots and duplicate/omit concurrent records?
Can a pinned main-store read handle, projection snapshot, or request-local query state return data older than the fixed Raft applied-index horizon captured for the request?
Do aggregates and list/detail endpoints disagree immediately after writes?
Can follower routing serve a strong read without sufficient leadership/quorum evidence?
